newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Communist chief arrested for "slander".
newsitem.headline: Chile's Communist chief arrested for "slander".

text.p: Police arrested the president of the Chilean Communist Party on slander charges on Tuesday after she called former military ruler Augusto Pinochet a blackmailer and a psychopath.

Armed plainclothes police agents stopped party chief Gladys Marin in her car and took her to a detention centre, police and Communist Party officials said. Pinochet's attorneys filed slander and defamation charges against Marin last month over statements she made about him at a memorial service for the roughly 3,200 people -- including Marin's husband -- killed by security forces during Pinochet's rule.

"I stand by everything I said. Pinochet has no right to sue me or any other Chilean," she managed to tell reporters as she was hustled out of a police car at a Santiago courthouse where hundreds of people gathered to rally in her support.
"I'm no common criminal and I have a right to my political opinions," she said. After appearing before a judge in a closed-door hearing, she was taken back to jail.

At the memorial service on Sept. 11, Marin called Pinochet "a blackmailer and a psychopath who came to power through deceit, treason and murder." She repeated the statement almost word-for-word last week and said the slander charges were themselves "an act of slander and an affront to the people of Chile, which struggled for so long to return to democracy."
Pinochet, 80, is still commander-in-chief of the army although he handed the presidency over to civilians in 1990. Chilean law bars "slander of the army forces."

Leaders of President Eduardo Frei's centre-left coalition government reacted angrily to the arrest. One said it tarnished Chile's image two weeks before about 20 heads of state were to arrive in Santiago for an Ibero-American summit.

"It's an outrage for Chilean democracy. When the army commander can get a political party leader arrested because of statements she made at a memorial service it's the world turned upside down," said Jorge Schaulsohn, president of the Party for Democracy, one of four parties in the coalition.

In a show of official support for Marin, Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco met Communist leaders in the Moneda presidential palace -- the very place bombed by Pinochet's forces in the 1973 coup that brought him to power.

Marin spent most of the Pinochet years in exile and has given the Communists a more combative voice in politics since becoming party chief in 1994. The party is not a member of Frei's coalition and has no representation in Congress.
The arrest order must have come from the judge but probably on the request of the plaintiff -- in this case, Pinochet, legal sources said.

Marin's associates sharply criticised the way she was arrested by a squad of armed police -- "as if she were a dangerous criminal," said Communist Party official Volodia Teitelboim. Marin had promised the judge she would appear for the hearing voluntarily, party officials said.
"They surrounded her and pulled her out of the car. It was a big scene. She looked like she was crying," a witness to the arrest said on state television.
